findings.title: In WebAssembly the repair profile leaves a container's word numbers in linear memory
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: recorded and fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Build for wasm32 and call `Card::new` or `Repaired::of`: the stack arrays `data`, `received`, `unreadable`, `corrected`, `sources` and `outputs` keep the container's and the card's word numbers after the call, because `stack::cleared` (secret-protection-core's `with_cleared_stack`) clears nothing in WebAssembly.
findings.expected: The module documentation says the values are cleared; elsewhere the crate wipes such stack values itself (`phrase::word_of`) or keeps them in a `Secret` (`password_check`).
findings.observed: The arrays are never wiped, and `src/repair/code.rs` claims clearing without the native-only exception that `lib.rs` states.
findings.impact: A WebAssembly host's linear memory keeps the word numbers of a container and its card until they are overwritten; native builds are not affected.
findings.recommendedFix: Hold the arrays in `zeroize::Zeroizing`, wiped on every path out, and say in the module documentation that stack clearing is native only.
findings.requiredVerification: The repair unit tests, the published repair vectors and the repair fuzz target pass.

findings.title: Seed::derive sends any passphrase's NFKD size to an allocation that ends the program
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: recorded and fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: On wasm32, `Seed::derive(&phrase, &"\u{FDFA}".repeat(70_000_000))`: the NFKD counts 2.31e9 bytes, above `isize::MAX`, and `Secret::zeroed` ends the instance.
findings.expected: RUST-17: a size is checked before it reaches an allocation, or the contract says what happens. `Password::new` refuses its limit with `PasswordTooLong`.
findings.observed: Nothing bounds or documents the passphrase's size beyond asking a host to bound text it reads from a file or the clipboard.
findings.impact: A host that passes an unbounded passphrase in WebAssembly ends its program; no memory safety or secret is at stake. The specification sets no passphrase limit.
findings.recommendedFix: State in `Seed::derive`'s documentation that a passphrase whose NFKD the memory cannot hold, never more than 2 GiB in WebAssembly, ends the program.
findings.requiredVerification: Documentation review; the new passphrase fuzz target compares the seed with bip39's.

findings.title: fuzz/Cargo.lock resolves other versions than Cargo.lock and no RustSec check reads it
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: recorded and fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Compare the two lockfiles: sha2 0.11.2, ctutils 0.4.8 and syn 3.0.10 in fuzz/Cargo.lock against 0.11.1, 0.4.6 and 3.0.9 in Cargo.lock; audit.yml reads Cargo.lock only.
findings.expected: The fuzz runs exercise the dependency graph the tests, the notices and RustSec see.
findings.observed: Three shared packages differ, and libfuzzer-sys, cc and the other fuzz-only crates get no advisory check in CI.
findings.impact: A release's 90-second fuzz runs test a slightly different graph; an advisory against a fuzz-only crate would go unnoticed in CI.
findings.recommendedFix: Pin the three packages to the root versions, and add a RustSec step and paths entry for fuzz/Cargo.lock.
findings.requiredVerification: No package shared by the two lockfiles differs; `cargo deny` and `cargo audit` pass for both; audit.yml lists fuzz/Cargo.lock.

findings.title: The Linux isolation test expects NoMemoryReading from the PID namespace alone
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: recorded and fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Run the isolation test in a user namespace its user owns without a new PID namespace (`unshare --user --map-current-user`): secret-protection-core 0.2.0 reports `Unknown`, and the test expects `Confirmed`.
findings.expected: Since secret-protection-core 0.2.0, NoMemoryReading is confirmed only for a program started in the first user namespace as well as the first PID namespace.
findings.observed: The test checks the PID namespace only, and asserts that the parent cannot open the child's memory, which it can in such a user namespace.
findings.impact: The test fails where the library is right; CI's runners start in the first user namespace, so no run failed.
findings.recommendedFix: Read the user namespace before the isolation and require both, as secret-protection-core's own test does; check the parent's refusal only in the first user namespace.
findings.requiredVerification: The isolation program passes on Linux; its expectations match secret-protection-core 0.2.0.

findings.title: The code-rules gate reads fuzz builds and corpora and counts no fuzz target's lines
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: recorded and fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: After any fuzz build, `cargo xtask code-rules` reads fuzz/target (generated Rust files among its hundreds of megabytes) and fuzz/corpus; COUNTED has no entry for fuzz/fuzz_targets/.
findings.expected: The gate skips build outputs and data, and CORE-15 counts every source file of the repository.
findings.observed: SKIPPED compares whole paths and skips only the root `target`; the fuzz targets are never measured; comments still call Cargo.lock the one lockfile, and the check's header omits the C++ compiler that linting the fuzz targets needs.
findings.impact: A slow gate that may report problems in generated files, and no line limit on the fuzz targets; no wrong pass today.
findings.recommendedFix: Skip fuzz/target, fuzz/corpus, fuzz/artifacts and fuzz/coverage, count fuzz/fuzz_targets/, and correct the comments.
findings.requiredVerification: `cargo xtask code-rules` passes after a fuzz build and names the fuzz targets' files.

findings.title: Recovery readings and the wallet check's passphrase have no fuzz target
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: recorded and fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: List the fuzz targets: phrase, password, repair, password_check. None reaches `Recovery::readings` with any stated length, or `Seed::derive` with a passphrase that `Password::new` would refuse (control characters, unassigned code points, over 1,024 bytes).
findings.expected: RUST-18: every parser and reader of untrusted input has a fuzz target.
findings.observed: Two inputs a person gives, a stated length and a passphrase, reach no fuzz target.
findings.impact: Inputs outside the unit tests' cases are not explored on these two paths.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a recovery target (a stand-in engine, any container, any stated length: each reading reads back, and is verified exactly when its length's verifier matched) and a passphrase target (the seed equals bip39's of the passphrase's NFKD). The phrase target also writes valid phrases as a person may, so that it reaches the checksum.
findings.requiredVerification: Each new target runs without a crash; the release workflow lists them through `cargo fuzz list`.

findings.title: Android and iOS run on no runner though an emulator and the simulator exist
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: recorded and fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: TARGETS.md and ci.yml at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Read RUST-16 against TARGETS.md: hosted Ubuntu runners can run an x86-64 Android emulator, and macOS runners the iOS simulator (`aarch64-apple-ios-sim`), which has no row.
findings.expected: RUST-16: only a target no available runner can run stays built and linted only; section 17.3 asks for a simulator row beside the device row, and a row for the fuzz build.
findings.observed: CI builds and lints Android and iOS only; TARGETS.md had no simulator or fuzz row, and its first paragraph passed 100 columns.
findings.impact: The crate's code on Android and iOS runs nowhere before a program built on it; little of it is specific to those systems.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the rows and the gap; run the tests that need no app process in an Android emulator and in the iOS simulator.
findings.requiredVerification: A CI job per emulator with a non-zero count of checks.

findings.title: SECURITY.md does not say that another process sees an operation's settings
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: recorded and fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: While Argon2id runs, read `/proc/PID/status` from another process of any user: VmRSS gives the memory level, and the time of each round the PIM, also after the dumpable flag is cleared.
findings.expected: The specification lets the settings be kept secret like part of the password, so the security policy says when they are visible.
findings.impact: A user who keeps the settings secret may expect them hidden from other processes.
findings.recommendedFix: One item under "What the crate cannot protect", naming Linux's `hidepid`.

findings.title: The clearing calls of the repair profile need 144 KiB of stack, above the documented 140
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: recorded and fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: docs/audits/AUD-006-harnesses/stack-need, run at the remediation commit.
findings.reproduction: Run docs/audits/AUD-006-harnesses/stack-need in the debug profile: `Card::new` and `Repaired::of` need 144 KiB on a thread of their own, as reed-solomon-core clears the stack inside the crate's own clearing.
findings.expected: The documented stack need holds for every public call that clears the stack.
findings.observed: The crate documents about 140 KiB; the repair calls need 144 KiB in the debug profile and 140 KiB in the release profile.
findings.impact: A host that sizes a thread at 140 KiB from the documents overflows it in a debug build.
findings.recommendedFix: Document up to 144 KiB, and name the repair calls as the deepest.
findings.requiredVerification: The harness passes against 144 KiB in both profiles.
